chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: “When you wash your deceased, then be gentle with him, do not wring him, do not press any joint of his, and do not bring any of the camphor near his ears. Then take his turban and spread it folded over his head, cast its two ends behind him, and leave his forehead exposed.”
I said: “As for the hanut, how should I apply it?” He said: “It is placed in his nostrils, on the places of his sajdah, and on his joints.”

I said: “Then the shroud?” He said: “A cloth is taken and his lower part is tied with it, and his thighs are drawn together with it so that what is there may be contained, and what is made of cotton is better. Then he is shrouded in a shirt, a wrapping cloth, and a mantle in which the shroud is gathered.”

key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt used as part of the shrouding
key_terms.لِفَافَةٍ: a wrapping cloth used in the shroud
key_terms.مَفَاصِلِهِ: his joints, mentioned as places for treatment and care
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِهِ: the places of prostration on the body where hanut is applied
key_terms.ٱلْحَنُوطُ: the perfuming substance applied to the deceased in prescribed places
key_terms.ٱلْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person being prepared for burial

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be washed, perfumed, and shrouded according to this hadith from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines rulings and etiquette for washing, perfuming, and shrouding the deceased. It emphasizes gentleness toward the dead body and gives specific instructions for applying hanut and arranging the kafan according to ritual practice.
